title: A two-era GJ 176 coherence test depends on the assumed noise for a 35 to 45 day extra wave
abstract: We test a common extra velocity wave in 117 public GJ 176 HARPS visits. A prior study found that a fixed early 40.32-day wave raised later prediction error but omitted early fit uncertainty. We compare common and separate-era sine coefficients after fitting frequency from 35 to 45 days in both models. Each era has its own offset, trend, 8.776-day planet wave and 39.34-day rotation wave. With 2 m/s added Gaussian error, the fit cost of coherence is 7.1865 and a 1999-draw parametric tail fraction is 0.0265. Added errors of 4 and 6 m/s give fractions of 0.2770 and 0.5245. Shared-sign residual tests with 1 to 100 day bins give 0.112 to 0.209. A finer grid and direct SVD fits check the calculation. Thus evidence against a common wave depends on the assumed noise. The test does not confirm a stable wave or overturn the prior fixed-wave prediction failure. The target and period range use prior knowledge. Unknown covariance, nearby rotation structure, a long gap and a change in HARPS limit interpretation. No independent instrument data or new planet are established. Code, aggregate profiles, synthetic scores, source hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included. Source database rows are excluded.

display.caption: The coherence cost and Gaussian null simulations depend on the added error scale. Dashed lines mark observed costs. All tests refit the extra frequency.

citations.reason: We test the fit-uncertainty limit stated by the fixed-wave prediction study with new frequency-profiled common and split fits.
External HARPS-RVBank version 02 source and attribution; raw database is excluded.
Its fixed-period seasonal test states a period-selection limit. We test a nearby extra wave with two eras and frequency fitting in every simulation.
